set.n: Horrigan brothers' farm money, Horrigan Ridge near Mt. Zion
set.pl: Horrigan Ridge (GNIS 1566706), sec. 35 T10N R3W, Crawford County, between Mt. Zion and Soldiers Grove. The exact farmstead needs a 1920s-30s Crawford plat.
set.st: Cornelius and Stephen Horrigan distrusted banks and were said to have hidden money around their farm, which the AP put about 17 miles from Boscobel. On 11 Nov 1930 three men posing as hunters, with a well-dressed woman, came to the farm. They had asked earlier for permission to hunt on it. They killed Patrick Gorman, 65, and his son Paul, 18, visitors from Huron, South Dakota, and wounded both brothers (Stephen was shot through the arm and Cornelius's jaw was shattered), but fled without searching. Their sister Ellen, 75, kept house. The case was worked from Prairie du Chien, and a suspect was arrested at a Wauzeka roadhouse. Neighbors said there were many stories of buried treasure on the homestead, and many people had dug over the farm. The summer before, three men and a woman had been run off it while digging. Two local papers place the farm: the Grant County Herald (12 Nov 1930) says 'the Horrigan farm near Mt. Zion', and the Muscoda Leader-Press (27 Nov 1930) says 'between Mt. Zion and Soldiers Grove'. GNIS has Horrigan Ridge about 5 km NE of Mt. Zion, about 12 miles in a straight line from Boscobel. The Herald names the brothers as William and Cornelius, while the AP has Stephen.
